subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should Skill Workshop own core-level failure-derived repair proposals and usage-based archive/retirement, or should maintainers first define a narrower plugin/API boundary for skill lifecycle metrics?
rationale: The request would add new public config, durable skill/session-derived state, ranking/archive/delete behavior, and possibly ClawHub telemetry, which is a product and ownership decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Define core lifecycle design first
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer design that splits failure repair from retirement and specifies state, consent, and UI/CLI boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Move to plugin/API discussion
options.body: Treat the feature as external lifecycle tooling and open only the missing plugin hooks or skill metrics APIs needed to support it outside core.

options.title: Defer retirement only
options.body: Accept failure-derived repair proposals as a smaller core extension while leaving archive/delete policy for a later user-approved lifecycle design.

recommendation.title: Define core lifecycle design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer design that splits failure repair from retirement and specifies state, consent, and UI/CLI boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent adjacent Skill Workshop/prompt work make this the strongest available owner for the product-boundary choice.
